Instance attunement refers to the process of gaining permanent access to an instance. The term comes from one of the first of such quests created: Attunement to the Core. Many of the endgame instances originally required you to complete a quest or obtain a certain item to enter. This strategy has largely been phased out, although some instances (particularly select mythic dungeons) still require attunement. * For a detailed look at attunement to the non-Burning Crusade instances, see Instance attunement (Classic). * For a detailed look at attunement to the Burning Crusade instances, see Instance attunement (Burning Crusade).

Instance bosses are bosses who spawn in an instance. These instances are tuned for raid-groups and vary in both level and difficulty. Before the The Burning Crusade expansion, the endgame raiding content was tuned to level 60 and to 40-man raidgroups. With the Burning Crusade expansion there came new endgame raiding content, tuned for level 70 players in 10- or 25-man raidgroups. Since all of these bosses require more then 5 players to defeat them, they are called raid bosses. The Instance Lock Extension feature allows players to continue an instance using a Raid ID that would normally have expired after its periodic reset, or has already expired - in other words, picking up from where they left off before the reset. This allows groups to progress through an instance at their own pace, instead of having to complete all of the content in one reset period in order to reach the end. The extension works on a per-player, per-lockout basis for any type of saved content, and can be reversed if a player has not significantly utilized it. Controls for the feature are found in the Raid Info popout within the Raid list window of the Social user interface pane.

For example, Onyxia's Lair is currently a Wrath of the Lich King raid, not Classic raid, and Zul'Gurub is a Cataclysm dungeon, not a Classic raid. An instant queue (also known as an insta-queue) is a tank or group that uses the Dungeon Finder to queue for a dungeon, and is immediately placed into the specific (or random) dungeon. Since a tank is the most highly demanded, and lowest supply, spec when using the dungeon finder, they typically can enter dungeons faster than say a healer or DPS can.

Invading Felguard are huge felguard that spawn from the Dark Portal in the Blasted Lands during the Dark Portal Opens event. They don't seem to drop any loot and despawn after they are killed. Killing 6 Invading Felguards is the objective of Into the Breach (Blasted Lands).

This article is about Blizzard introducing the Tinfoil Hat. The Tinfoil Hat is a fictional item in World of Warcraft that was announced on April 1, 2007. The announcement was a satiric response to player concerns raised by the launch of World of Warcraft Armory, a part of the Blizzard website displaying all characters' equipment and talent choices. While the most obvious part of the story parodies X-Files themes; names of characters in the screenshots – Sparta, Xerxes, Gorgo, Leonidas, Delios, Sunblot, Shadowfight, and Helldiner – are related to the movie 300, a possible response to a rise in Sparta-related quotes on the forums shortly after the movie's theatrical premiere. Invoke the Light is a Discipline priest artifact trait. It is linked to the Light's Wrath (artifact trait), Confession and Shield of Faith traits.

Invasion Points (or Argus Rifts) are worlds targeted by an invasion of the Burning Legion. The portal network on Argus allows adventurers to access them, using riftstones from Kil'jaeden's ship. The goal is to clear out the Legion invasion force, fight a boss, do an event, and complete an objective.

Invasive Gazers are observers located in Invasion Point: Bonich.

The party leader, or raid assistant can **invite** other players to join the group. This can be done in a number of ways: * Using the /invite slash command. * By selecting a player, right-clicking their portrait, and selecting invite. * Using the Friends List window, selecting the player character's name, and clicking the appropriate button on the lower right. Other group members may use the above methods to suggest players for the group leader to invite.
